extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants (issuers), their accountants, auditors, and securities lawyers/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance for preparing and reporting climate-related disclosures in SEC filings (Regulation S-K subpart 1500 and Regulation S-X Article 14), including financial-statement note disclosures, PRA burden estimation, phase-in and assurance requirements, and special treatment for small reporting companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Paperwork burden estimates are based in part on the BEIS impact assessment for the UK climate disclosure rules, the 2021 FCA cost-benefit analysis, input from commenters, and other direct cost estimates discussed in the Economic Analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These direct cost estimates are treated as a reasonable means of determining the estimated collection of information burden and likely represent an upper bound because the approach is conservative (erring on the side of overstating costs rather than understating them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multi-year averaging for PRA burden
rubrics_metrics.description: For PRA purposes, the Commission typically calculates a three-year average, but estimated a nine-year average for these final rules because one amendment's requirement will not be phased in until the ninth year of initially providing the disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate burdens as an average over the applicable phase-in span (here nine years) to capture initial implementation and later compliance steps (e.g., assurance in year nine).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of burden between internal hours and outside professional costs (PRA Table 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard percentage estimates allocate burden between internal burden hours and outside professional costs for each affected collection of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Forms S-1, F-1, S-4, F-4, S-11, 10, and 20-F: internal 25% / outside professionals 75%; Form 10-K: internal 75% / outside professionals 25%. Apply these allocations when converting cost estimates to internal and external burden hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion rates for cost-to-hour calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert monetary cost estimates into burden hours using specified hourly conversion rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use $441/hr to convert costs to internal burden hours for governance, strategy and risk management, scenario analysis, Scopes 1 and 2 emissions, targets and goals, and financial statement disclosures. Use $600/hr to convert external professional costs into burden hours. Round all numbers to the nearest whole number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of materiality qualifiers and disclosure category changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules include materiality qualifiers and revisions to disclosure categories, e.g., separating targets from metrics and replacing 'financial statement metrics' with 'financial statement disclosures'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality qualifiers and these category adjustments reduce the estimated burden relative to the proposed rules; they reflect that disclosures will depend on particular facts and circumstances and thus will not be required from all registrants in all instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in schedule for Scopes 1 and 2 emissions disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase-in varies by registrant group: Large Accelerated Filers (LAFs) and non-exempt Accelerated Filers (AFs that are not SRCs or EGCs) are subject to the requirement to disclose Scopes 1 and 2 emissions if material, with LAFs complying beginning in their second fiscal year of compliance and non-exempt AFs beginning in their third fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables estimating paperwork burden span nine years to capture the phased compliance and later assurance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attestation requirement timing and assurance level
rubrics_metrics.description: After a three-year phased-in compliance period for reporting GHG emissions, both LAFs and non-exempt AFs will be required to obtain an attestation report to verify their GHG emissions disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LAFs will initially be required to obtain an attestation report at the limited assurance level, and after a four-year transition period they will be required to obtain an attestation report at the reasonable assurance level. Reasonable assurance is expected to be more costly than limited assurance; burden estimates include separate tables for attestation-related effects over a nine-year span.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate of percentage of filers affected
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a certain percentage of filers of each form are estimated to be required to provide climate-related disclosures, because the rules include materiality qualifiers and depend on registrants' facts and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate affected percentages using third-party surveys of current disclosure practices, commenters' estimates, and staff estimates; use these percentages when calculating the number of affected respondents and incremental burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure thresholds for financial statement effects (§210.14-02(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Thresholds determine when specific financial statement disclosures are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For expenditures expensed as incurred and losses (paragraph (c)): disclose if the aggregate amount equals or exceeds 1% of the absolute value of income or loss before income tax expense or benefit for the relevant fiscal year, except no disclosure required if aggregate amount is less than $100,000. For capitalized costs and charges (paragraph (d)): disclose if the aggregate amount equals or exceeds 1% of the absolute value of stockholders' equity or deficit at the end of the fiscal year, except no disclosure required if absolute amount is less than $500,000.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual information requirement for financial statement effects (§210.14-02(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contextual information describing how each specified financial statement effect was derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a description of significant inputs and assumptions used, significant judgments made, other information important to understand the financial statement effect, and, if applicable, policy decisions made by the registrant to calculate the specified disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of calculation for Article 14 disclosures (§210.14-01(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating financial statement effects in Article 14, use financial information consistent with the scope of the consolidated financial statements and apply the same accounting principles required for preparing those consolidated financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same measurement bases, consolidation scope, and accounting policies used in the audited consolidated financial statements included in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods to be disclosed for Article 14 (§210.14-01(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure must be provided for the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year and, to the extent previously disclosed or required, for the historical fiscal year(s) for which audited consolidated financial statements are included in the filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comparable historical periods consistent with the audited statements presented in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and applicability of Article 14 disclosures (§210.14-01(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must include Article 14 disclosure in any filing that is required to include disclosure pursuant to subpart 229.1500 and that also requires inclusion of audited financial statements; the Article 14 disclosure must be included in a note to the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only apply Article 14 disclosures in filings that both trigger Item 1500-related disclosures and contain audited consolidated financial statements; present the disclosures as a financial-statement note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation instructions for expenditures and capitalized costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclose and separately identify where the expenditures expensed as incurred and losses are presented in the income statement, and separately identify where capitalized costs and charges are presented in the balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear mapping to financial-statement line items so users can locate the effects in the audited statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon offsets and RECs disclosure (§210.14-02(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If carbon offsets or renewable energy certificates (RECs) have been used as a material component of a registrant's plans to achieve disclosed climate-related targets or goals, disclose aggregate amounts and balances related to those instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose the aggregate amount of offsets and RECs expensed, aggregate amount of capitalized offsets and RECs recognized, aggregate amount of losses incurred on capitalized offsets and RECs, and the beginning and ending balances of the capitalized offsets and RECs for the fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternatives to minimize impacts on small entities (RFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: In conducting the Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis, the Commission considered alternatives that would accomplish the rule's objectives while minimizing adverse impacts on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives considered include: exempting small entities from all or part of the requirements; establishing different compliance or reporting requirements for small entities; using performance rather than design standards; and clarifying, consolidating, or simplifying compliance and reporting requirements for small entities. The Commission explains which alternatives were not adopted and why, and which mitigations (e.g., phase-ins, exemptions) were adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions, phase-in, and special treatment for smaller registrants
rubrics_metrics.description: SRCs, EGCs, and NAFs receive special treatment: they are not subject to the requirement to disclose Scope 1 and 2 emissions, are excluded from Scope 3 disclosures (the Commission is not adopting Scope 3), and are excluded from certain GHG attestation requirements. They are also provided longer phase-in periods (earliest compliance filings required to include FY2027 financial information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These carve-outs and extended compliance dates are intended to reduce burdens on smaller reporting companies while still advancing investor information objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of performance and design standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules incorporate a combination of performance and design standards to balance uniform requirements and registrant flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use design standards to promote uniform compliance and address disclosure concerns, while incorporating elements of performance standards and providing a non-exhaustive list of examples registrants should include where applicable, rather than prescribing a more prescriptive set of disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of variability in burdens across firms
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission recognizes that burdens and costs will vary among registrants based on firm characteristics (size, industry, business model, corporate complexity, starting level of expertise, etc.) and that compliance costs may be proportionally greater for smaller companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account firm-specific factors when assessing materiality, whether disclosure is required, and when estimating burdens; acknowledge uncertainty and variability in economic impact estimates.
